title: Investment firm RMBV to acquire 50% stake in Egypt's ATCO Pharma
summary: The transaction is valued at $50 million

contentHtml:
Skyline over the Nile in Cairo before sunset, aerial view, Egypt. Image used for illustrative purpose. Image courtesy: Getty Images/ Anton Alexsenko

The transaction is valued at $50 million

North Africa-focused investment firm RMBV has signed an agreement to acquire a 50% stake in local drugmaker ATCO Pharma through its RNAF III fund for $50 million, a source familiar with the transaction told Zawya.

Zilla Capital acted as the sole financial adviser to ATCO.

The transaction will see RMBV acquire a combination of newly issued and existing shares in ATCO Pharma.

The investment will support ATCO’s plans to expand its range of human and veterinary medicines, develop new products and enter additional regional markets.

ATCO manufactures more than 150 pharmaceutical products and exports to over 10 countries, including Saudi Arabia and Nepal. The company also has more than 160 drug compounds under development.

While the deal value was not disclosed, the transaction represents RMBV's maiden investment in Egypt's veterinary pharmaceuticals industry.

RMBV has invested more than $1 billion to date through various funds across healthcare, education, consumer goods and financial services in Egypt and the wider North African region. The firm has also returned more than $1.5 billion to investors through 13 exits.

(Reporting by Ahmad Mousa; editing by Seban Scaria)
